title: Taskified Admin Quickflows: lightweight task runner for ad-hoc support flows
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Summary: Build 'Quickflows' — a compact, task-first runner for common admin and support flows (user-scoped DB migrations, cache clears, token rotations, customer-scoped data exports). Quickflows are designed to be authored as small, parameterized tasks (YAML/TS templates) and executed by on-call/support engineers via the admin console or CLI with guaranteed audit trails and safe guards.

Goals:
- Reduce time-to-resolution for common support actions by 40% through reusable task templates.
- Enforce safety: idempotency checks, preflight validation, and RBAC-controlled execution with full audit logs.
- Integrate with existing ops orchestration (playbook runner) without introducing a separate microservice.
- Provide dry-run and canary execution modes, plus automatic gating (circuit breaker) for risky steps.

Non-goals:
- Replacing long-running, multi-step incident runbooks (those remain in the orchestrator). Quickflows are for short, repeatable admin flows (<120s expected runtime).

Scope & Features:
1) Task format: compact YAML or TypeScript script that defines inputs, validation schema, and steps. Steps are idempotent primitives (SQL, HTTP, CLI, internal SDK calls).
2) Execution surface: admin console (Operations -> Quickflows) + admin-cli subcommand (admin quickflow run).
3) Safety primitives: pre-check functions, required approvals for high-risk flows, concurrency locks, rate limits, and a retry/backoff policy.
4) Auditing: immutable execution record per run (who/when/params/outputs), stored in events table and surfaced in Console.
5) Access control: maps to SSO groups/roles (support, infra, security); ephemeral elevated tokens for sensitive actions with KMS/HSM-backed signing.
6) Telemetry & monitoring: per-flow success/failure, median latency, and broken-down error classes emitted to the ops dashboard.

Architecture decisions (summary):
- Extend the existing admin-service runbook module rather than shipping a standalone Quickflows service. That reduces operational surface area and leverages existing tracing/observability hooks.
- Tasks run in a sandboxed worker pool with restricted network egress; long-running steps are disallowed by default.
- Use prefix-based KV caching where applicable to accelerate repeated lookups.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Whether to support Templated JS tasks (higher flexibility, more attack surface) vs declarative YAML steps (safer, less flexible). Initial rollout will allow only declarative YAML with parameterized SQL/HTTP/SDK steps; we will revisit JS tasks after security review.
- How to surface cost to users for tasks that invoke heavy inference (we'll add per-run cost estimate to preflight for any model-serving steps).

Rollout plan:
- Phase 0 (internal alpha): implement read-only task preview + dry-run, limited to infra and SRE (1 week).
- Phase 1 (canary): enable run for 10% of support org, monitor errors and SLOs for 2 weeks.
- Phase 2 (GA): open to full support org and select customer success engineers after security sign-off.

Metrics to validate success:
- Mean time to resolution (MTTR) for common support tickets — target: -40% at 30 days.
- Execution error rate < 2% on canary.
- No escalation incidents caused by Quickflows during canary (incident window).

Security & compliance notes:
- All sensitive parameters encrypted at rest using KMS; execution logs scrub secrets before storage.
- Required security review from Cloud Security; KMS/HSM integration must be validated before Phase 1.

Links & artifacts:
- Spec + examples: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Quickflows+Spec
- Prototype repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-quickflows (branch: feat/task-runner)
- PR (initial implementation): https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-quickflows/pull/1234
- Console mockups: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1q2w3e_quickflows-mockup/view
- Monitoring dashboard (dev): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/ops-quickflows/dev-dashboard

Acceptance criteria:
- Admin console shows Quickflows list with author and last-run metadata.
- Tasks can be executed in dry-run and live modes from console and CLI.
- Execution records emitted to events table and visible in Console with parameter redaction.
- RBAC enforced: only permitted groups can execute sensitive flows.
- Security review sign-off for KMS integration completed.
comments: 2026-03-02 - Ava Chen: Initial spec drafted and shared in #ops-tooling. Focus on short, repeatable admin flows. Asked SRE for input on worker pool sizing.
2026-03-04 - Diego Martinez: Architecture review scheduled. Proposal: extend admin-service runbook module to avoid new infra. Posting preliminary sequence diagram in Confluence.
2026-03-05 - Priya Nambiar (SRE): Confirmed worker pool approach is fine; suggested adding concurrency locks and tenant-scoped rate limits. Pointed out need to limit outbound egress for steps.
2026-03-06 - Security (review): Flagged requirement: initial rollout must disallow JS tasks. KMS integration and parameter scrubbing mandatory before canary. Added security checklist to Confluence.

2026-03-08 - Diego Martinez: Created prototype PR with YAML task runner and CLI hook (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/ops-quickflows/pull/1234). Basic dry-run passes unit tests. Requesting code review from infra and security.

2026-03-09 - PM feedback (Lena Ortiz): Requested UX changes: show estimated impact (latency/cost) in preflight and require explicit approval for actions affecting customer data. Added to acceptance criteria.

2026-03-11 - Diego Martinez: Integration tests failing intermittently under high concurrency (test: test_concurrent_locking). Root cause: lock TTL too short. Increasing TTL in worker pool config; adding deterministic test to reproduce race.
2026-03-12 - Ava Chen: Merged updated locking logic into feature branch. Next: schedule security review meeting and plan canary target group.
